editorial.headline: Sharia Pawn Activity, With a Clear National and Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 64954 covers sharia-based pawn activity, from secured lending and valuation to the safekeeping of valuables, and is open to foreign investment nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 64954 is the category for pawn activity conducted wholly under sharia principles. Its scope is broader than the simple image of an item exchanged for cash: it includes lending secured under pawn law, lending secured by fiduciary collateral, the safekeeping of valuable goods, and appraisal services. The defining feature is not one particular item or customer, but that the entire activity is organised on sharia principles.

The category also describes a sharia pawn business whose core work includes those same forms of secured lending, custody and valuation. It can encompass commission-based activities that are unrelated to pawn operations where they do not conflict with financial-services laws and regulations, as well as other business activities with the approval of the Financial Services Authority. That makes the classification precise about its centre of gravity: secured finance, valuables handling and appraisal, all within a sharia operating model.

The activity is open at every listed business scale: micro, small, medium and large. Nationally, it is marked open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record presents no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The stated national basis is Presidential Regulation 10/2021 and 49/2021.

Bali does not change that result into a prohibition. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for activities assessed as Low or Medium-Low risk across the island, but this activity is recorded as not blocked by that moratorium. At the large-business scale, its OSS risk classification is Medium-High/High, which is why the Bali record places it in the “OK_or_HIGHER_RISK” position rather than treating it as moratorium-blocked. For a foreign investor considering sharia pawn activity in Bali, the honest reading is straightforward: the code is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and is not barred from PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium rule.
